body:
A Rust `submit` that fails to parse names neither the block nor where the item was placed. In task:1ba2b996f1282bbb run `a348af56b1f15298` the first reply was `line 28: cannot parse string into token stream: }` (no block, no file); the retry named a temp file `.solace/format-<hash>.rs:28`. The agent spent a long turn guessing which of four blocks was at fault, when the cause was the item being wrapped in the wrong container.

Gleam's errors are located by symbol; Rust's should be too.

1. When `cargo::format_item` or the `syn` parse in `store.submit_items` fails, report the block's header name (`<module>.<name>`) and the line within the submitted text, not within the wrapper or temp file.
2. When the item was wrapped in a container (an `impl`, `trait` or inline `mod`), say so: "added inside `<container qname>` (<kind>)", so a wrong placement is visible.
3. Never show the `.solace/format-*.rs` path; drop the bare "cannot parse string into token stream" form for the located one.
4. Tests: a multi-block submit with one bad block names that block and its own line; an `*** Add` placed in an inline `mod` names the container; no reply contains `.solace/format-`.

Checks: `rust-unit`, `rust-acceptance`.

Left out: fixing container placement itself (note 2 on task:1ba2b996f1282bbb).
title: submit: Rust syntax errors name the block
